reviews.overall: Em cần sửa và nộp lại bài này. Bài em làm còn ẩu ở các lỗi cơ bản lặp lại: “the UK started”, “Belgium also rise” dùng tên nước làm thứ tăng, còn “fall” và “rise” chưa chia quá khứ. Overview thiếu thông tin thấp nhất; phần Belgium chưa thể hiện diễn biến chính sau năm 2004. Em đã dùng quy chiếu và các cụm mở rộng, nhưng cần dùng đúng trong từng câu. Đi học là để ghi chép, hiểu và vận dụng lại kiến thức để tự viết. Cô yêu cầu em tự chữa các câu đã đánh dấu và rút bài về đúng độ dài.
reviews.dataGrouping: Detail 1 của em gồm Germany–Italy; Detail 2 gồm France–UK–Belgium, theo đúng thứ tự này. Cách chia hợp lý theo thứ hạng cuối kỳ; France đứng đầu năm 2004 nên không gọi Germany–Italy là nhóm cao nhất suốt giai đoạn. Cô giữ nhóm và thứ tự của em, rút các mốc chưa cần thiết và bổ sung diễn biến của Belgium.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line graph illustrates the percentages of female members of parliament in five European countries between 2000 and 2012.

Overall, there was a general increase in the percentages of female members of parliament in Germany, Italy, and the UK; however, the figures in France and Belgium went down at some points. Also of note is that the UK witnessed the most noticeable increase, while Germany consistently had the highest figures in the first years.

To elaborate, in 2000, the percentage of female members of parliament was around 33% in Germany, with a more noticeable upturn to approximately 35% in 2004. However, in 2012, that figure went up to around 37%. Regarding Italy, the figure started at 27% in 2000 and rose to 31% in 2004, before growing to 33% in 2008 and 39% in 2012, marking the highest point of the entire graph.

Conversely, the figure for France increased considerably from 25% in 2000 to around 37% in 2004, but later fall to 29% in 2008 before growing again to 31% in 2012. Regarding categories with lower data, the UK started at only 3% in 2000 and increased considerably to 28% in 2012. Belgium also rise from around 17% to 28% over the same period.

Overall, the percentages of female members of parliament increased in all five countries, most sharply in the United Kingdom, despite some declines in France and Belgium. Germany led initially and Italy finished highest, while the United Kingdom remained lowest, equalling Belgium in 2012.

To elaborate, in 2000, around 33% of German parliament members were women, with a subsequent slight rise to 37% in 2012. The figure for Italy also increased, but more markedly, from approximately 26% to 39% over the same period.

Conversely, the percentage of female members of parliament in France rose from 25% in 2000 to a peak of 37% in 2004, the highest figure that year, before falling and recovering to 31% in 2012. The figure for the United Kingdom climbed from 3% to 28% between 2000 and 2012. Similarly, that for Belgium rose from 17% to 28% by 2004, after which it remained relatively stable until 2012.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given pie charts illustrates the main reasons why students chose a particular university in the UK in 1997 and 2007.

Overall, there was a general increase in suitable degree courses, proximity to parental home, and quality of teaching; however, the figures for quality of resources and good sports and social activities went down. Also of note is that suitable degree courses consistently had the highest figures in both years.

To elaborate, in 1997, the percentage of students choosing suitable degree courses was 35%, with a slight upturn to 37% in 2007, marking the highest point of both charts. Regarding quality of resources, the figure started at 21% in 1997 and fell to 17% in 2007. The figures for proximity to parental home was 10% in 1997, before rising considerably to 22% in 2007.

Conversely, the percentage for quality of teaching increased from 15% in 1997 to 18% in 2007. Regarding categories with lower data, good sports and social activities started at 19% in 1997, but later fell considerably to only 6% in 2007. The figure for suitable degree courses also increase slightly between the two years.

Regarding the remaining countries, the figures for Biology, Medicine and Psychology in Australia were 9, 13 and 17 respectively, with the figure for Psychology being the highest. A similar pattern was seen in Canada, with the figures for the three subjects being 9, 12 and 14 respectively. Meanwhile, New Zealand had the lowest figures overall, with only 6 universities in Biology, 2 in Medicine and 4 in Psychology.
